modules.name: lib/skyrme/skyrmehf
modules.src:
# Skyrme Hartree-Fock of a spherical closed-shell nucleus, as a program with
# its settings at the top level: the nucleus, the force (one of four, or its
# ten parameters given one by one), the mesh, and the iteration's mixing,
# tolerance and limit. It runs lib/skyrme/spherical's solver once and copies
# what it finds into the globals below the run.
#
#     viv run lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.viv
#     viv export lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.export.toml     (one C file and a Python wrapper)
#
# The orbitals are filled by energy, lowest first, across every (n, l, j); a
# nucleus whose last orbital would be partly filled is refused (the solver
# has no pairing). Oxygen-16, calcium-40 and -48, nickel-56, zirconium-90,
# tin-132 and lead-208 are closed in both kinds.
#
# The defaults are oxygen-16 with SLy5 on 150 points of 0.1 fm, the
# settings of lib/skyrme/story_o16.viv and of the post's first mesh
# (posts/2026-09-25-skyrme-hartree-fock-of-oxygen-16.viv); a run with no
# settings changed gives lib/skyrme/skyrme's bits, and the post's numpy twin
# to 1e-7 (tools/export/test_skyrmehf.py checks it).
from scf.mix import MixDensities, MixHistory, MixStep, broyden, linear, mix_densities, pulay
from skyrme.spherical import Force, SIII, SKMS, SLY4, SLY5, nucleus_n, nucleus_z, solve_with
from skyrme.skyrme import NEUTRON, PROTON, particle_number

#: SkyrmeName  the forces the program has
enum SkyrmeName {
    Sly4
    Sly5
    Siii
    Skms
}

#: NUCLEUS  the nucleus: its mass number and element, as "208Pb" (or "Pb208", "pb-208")
NUCLEUS: Str = "16O"
#: FORCE  the Skyrme force: SLy4, SLy5, SIII or SkM*; T0 ... J2 below start from its values
FORCE = SkyrmeName.Sly5

preset = SLY5
match FORCE {
    Sly4 => {
        preset = SLY4
    }
    Sly5 => {
        preset = SLY5
    }
    Siii => {
        preset = SIII
    }
    Skms => {
        preset = SKMS
    }
}

# ---- the force's parameters: FORCE's, unless given
#: T0  the force's t0, MeV fm^3
T0 = preset.t0
#: T1  the force's t1, MeV fm^5
T1 = preset.t1
#: T2  the force's t2, MeV fm^5
T2 = preset.t2
#: T3  the force's t3, MeV fm^(3 + 3 ALPHA)
T3 = preset.t3
#: X0  the force's x0, the spin exchange of the t0 term
X0 = preset.x0
#: X1  the force's x1, the spin exchange of the t1 term
X1 = preset.x1
#: X2  the force's x2, the spin exchange of the t2 term
X2 = preset.x2
#: X3  the force's x3, the spin exchange of the t3 term
X3 = preset.x3
#: W0  the spin-orbit strength, MeV fm^5
W0 = preset.w0
#: ALPHA  the power of the density in the t3 term
ALPHA = preset.alpha
#: J2  whether the J^2 terms of t1 and t2 are kept (SLy5 and SIII keep them, SLy4 and SkM* drop them)
J2 = preset.j2

Z_NUC = nucleus_z(NUCLEUS)
N_NUC = nucleus_n(NUCLEUS)

# ---- the mesh: r_i = (i + 1) SPACING for i below round(BOX / SPACING)
#: SPACING  the mesh spacing, fm
SPACING = 0.1
#: BOX  the width of the box, fm: the orbitals are zero past it. The default grows with the nucleus: 15 fm, or 1.2 A^(1/3) + 11.5 fm when that is wider (18.6 fm for lead-208)
BOX = max(15.0, 1.2 * pow(Z_NUC + N_NUC, 1.0 / 3.0) + 11.5)

# ---- the iteration
#: MIXING  how the next pass's densities are made (lib/scf/mix): pulay, the
#:     default, and broyden combine the last HISTORY passes; linear keeps MIX
#:     of the new densities and needs more passes; every runs all three on
#:     each pass, checks that they see the same residual, and continues with
#:     pulay's densities (the contract's default)
MIXING = MixDensities.Pulay
#: MIX  the fraction of each pass's new densities mixed into the old ones;
#:     pulay and broyden take this fraction of their combined residual
MIX = 0.5
#: HISTORY  how many passes pulay and broyden combine, the current one
#:     included; pulay and broyden only, ignored by linear
HISTORY: Int = 6
#: E_TOL  the iteration stops when the energy changes by less than this between passes, MeV
E_TOL = 1.0e-9
#: MAX_ITER  at most this many passes
MAX_ITER = 300

using mix_densities = MIXING
settings linear(alpha = MIX)
settings pulay(alpha = MIX, history = HISTORY)
settings broyden(alpha = MIX, history = HISTORY)

#: x_in  the densities a pass started from, packed (lib/skyrme/spherical)
#: x_out  the densities the pass produced
#: hist  the earlier passes the mixer remembers
#: x_next  the densities the next pass starts from
#: hist_next  the history the next call is given
#: residual  the largest |x_out - x_in|
#| One mixing step by the method MIXING selects.
#@ f44d5be6
def mixer(x_in: Arr, x_out: Arr, hist: MixHistory) -> MixStep {
    x_next, hist_next, residual = mix_densities(x_in, x_out, hist)
    return MixStep { x: x_next, hist: hist_next, residual: residual }
}

hf_force = Force { t0: T0, t1: T1, t2: T2, t3: T3, x0: X0, x1: X1, x2: X2, x3: X3, w0: W0, alpha: ALPHA, j2: J2 }
hf_res = solve_with(SPACING, round(BOX / SPACING), hf_force, Z_NUC, N_NUC, mixer, E_TOL, MAX_ITER)

# ---- what the run found
#: Z  the protons
Z: Int = round(Z_NUC)
#: N  the neutrons
N: Int = round(N_NUC)
#: E_PER_A  the energy per nucleon, MeV
E_PER_A = hf_res.e_per_a
#: ENERGY  the total energy, MeV
ENERGY = hf_res.energy
#: R_P  the protons' root mean square radius, fm
R_P = hf_res.r_p
#: R_N  the neutrons' root mean square radius, fm
R_N = hf_res.r_n
#: R_CH  the charge radius: the proton density folded with a Gaussian of range 0.65 fm, fm
R_CH = hf_res.r_ch
#: LEVELS  the occupied orbitals' energies, MeV: the neutrons' lowest first, then the protons'
LEVELS = hf_res.levels
#: LABELS  the names of LEVELS, comma-separated: "n 1s1/2,n 1p3/2,...,p 1s1/2,..."
LABELS = hf_res.labels
#: SPECTRUM  every bound orbital of the converged fields, MeV: the neutrons' lowest first, then the protons'
SPECTRUM = hf_res.spectrum
#: SPECTRUM_LABELS  the names of SPECTRUM, comma-separated
SPECTRUM_LABELS = hf_res.spectrum_labels
#: SPECTRUM_OCC  the nucleons in each SPECTRUM orbital: 2j + 1 if occupied, else 0
SPECTRUM_OCC = hf_res.spectrum_occ
#: ITERATIONS  the passes run
ITERATIONS = hf_res.iterations
#: CONVERGED  whether the energy settled to E_TOL within MAX_ITER passes
CONVERGED = hf_res.converged
#: REFILLS  the passes after the first in which the occupation was chosen again, because an orbital changed places
REFILLS = hf_res.refills
#: MESH  the mesh points, fm
MESH = hf_res.r
#: RHO  the number densities, fm^-3, [2, round(BOX / SPACING)]: row 0 neutrons, row 1 protons
RHO = hf_res.rho
#: TAU  the kinetic-energy densities, fm^-5, [2, round(BOX / SPACING)]
TAU = hf_res.tau
#: JSO  the spin-orbit densities, fm^-4, [2, round(BOX / SPACING)]
JSO = hf_res.jso

print(NUCLEUS, "Z", Z, "N", N)
print("E/A (MeV)", E_PER_A)
print("radii of the protons, the neutrons and the charge (fm)", R_P, R_N, R_CH)
print("occupied orbitals", LABELS)
print("their energies (MeV)", LEVELS)
print("passes", ITERATIONS, "converged", CONVERGED)

test "the energy settled to E_TOL within MAX_ITER passes" {
    assert_true(CONVERGED)
}
test "the densities hold N neutrons and Z protons" {
    assert_near(particle_number(RHO, NEUTRON, MESH, SPACING), N, 1.0e-9 * N)
    assert_near(particle_number(RHO, PROTON, MESH, SPACING), Z, 1.0e-9 * Z)
}

modules.src:
###
post: Skyrme Hartree-Fock of oxygen-16 on a radial mesh
agent: claude

The solver of posts/2026-09-25-skyrme-hartree-fock-of-oxygen-16.viv as a
module, with its self-consistent loop cut into steps and its fields and
single-particle Hamiltonian in defs of their own, so the explorer can walk
through it. The arithmetic is the post's, operation for operation: the story
beside this file (lib/skyrme/story_o16.viv) gets the post's numbers on its
0.1 fm mesh.

    from skyrme.skyrme import skyrme_o16

    res = skyrme_o16(0.1, 150)
    show res.e_per_a       # E/A, MeV

skyrme_o16 solves with SLy5 and the iteration settings below;
`skyrme_hf(h, nr, force, mix, e_tol, max_iter)` takes them as arguments,
the force as a SkyrmeForce record (SLY5 is one).
lib/skyrme/spherical.viv generalizes it to any spherical closed-shell
nucleus and four forces, with the same bits for oxygen-16 and SLy5; its
program lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.viv is what lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.export.toml
exports as one C file and a Python wrapper (`viv export`).

The force is SLy5 (Chabanat et al., Nucl. Phys. A 643, 441 (1998)) with
the parameters and constants of skyrme_rpa (Colò, Cao, Van Giai and
Capelli, Computer Physics Communications 184, 142 (2013)). The nucleus is
oxygen-16: 8 protons and 8 neutrons filling the $1s_{1/2}$, $1p_{3/2}$ and
$1p_{1/2}$ shells of each, so it is spherical and each orbital is the
lowest of its $(l, j)$ block. Each block's radial equation for $u(r) = r R(r)$ is a symmetric
tridiagonal matrix on the mesh $r_i = (i + 1) h$; its lowest eigenvector
comes from inverse iteration.

Used with `import skyrme.skyrme`.
###

# ---- SLy5, as skyrme_rpa's skyrme.in lists it (MeV and fm)
T0 = -2484.88
T1 = 483.13
T2 = -549.40
T3 = 13763.0
X0 = 0.778
X1 = -0.328
X2 = -1.0
X3 = 1.267
W0 = 126.0
ALPHA = 1.0 / 6.0

#| A Skyrme force: the ten parameters of the functional. t0 is in MeV fm^3,
#| t1, t2 and w0 in MeV fm^5, t3 in MeV fm^(3 + 3 alpha); the x's and alpha
#| have no unit. The J^2 terms are always included, as in SLy5.
record SkyrmeForce {
    t0: Num
    t1: Num
    t2: Num
    t3: Num
    x0: Num
    x1: Num
    x2: Num
    x3: Num
    w0: Num
    alpha: Num
}
SLY5 = SkyrmeForce { t0: T0, t1: T1, t2: T2, t3: T3, x0: X0, x1: X1, x2: X2, x3: X3, w0: W0, alpha: ALPHA }

# ---- skyrme_rpa's constants: hbar c, the nucleon mass (the p-n average), e^2
HBARC = 197.327053
M_NUC = 0.5 * (938.27231 + 939.56563)
E2 = 1.43986
PI = 3.141592653589793

# ---- oxygen-16
Z_P = 8
N_N = 8
A_NUC = Z_P + N_N
# the two kinds of nucleon, as the first index of the density arrays
NEUTRON = 0
PROTON = 1
NKIND = 2
# the center-of-mass correction: hbar^2/2m times (1 - 1/A)
HB = HBARC * HBARC / (2.0 * M_NUC) * (1.0 - 1.0 / A_NUC)
# the occupied shells of each kind: l, j and the number of nucleons 2j + 1
SHELL_L = [0, 1, 1]
SHELL_J = [0.5, 1.5, 0.5]
# where 1p3/2 and 1p1/2 sit in that list
SHELL_P32 = 1
SHELL_P12 = 2
# the Gaussian range of the proton charge in skyrme_rpa's charge density (fm)
FOLD = 0.65
# the starting Woods-Saxon profile: radius R0 A^(1/3) and diffuseness (fm)
WS_R0 = 1.2
WS_DIFFUSE = 0.6

# ---- the iteration
MIX = 0.5
E_TOL = 1.0e-9
MAX_ITER = 300
# the energy must be settled after at least this many iterations
MIN_ITER = 3
# in the first iteration bisection brackets each orbital energy to EIG_TOL (MeV); after it the
# inverse-iteration shift is NEAR below the orbital's last energy. INV_SWEEPS solves per iteration.
EIG_TOL = 1.0e-11
NEAR = 0.1
INV_SWEEPS = 3

def grad1(f: Arr, h) {
    n = len(f)
    out = zeros(n)
    out[0] = (-1.5 * f[0] + 2.0 * f[1] - 0.5 * f[2]) / h
    out[1:n - 1] = (f[2:n] - f[0:n - 2]) / (2.0 * h)
    out[n - 1] = (1.5 * f[n - 1] - 2.0 * f[n - 2] + 0.5 * f[n - 3]) / h
    return out
}

def lap_r(f: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    d1 = grad1(f, h)
    return grad1(d1, h) + 2.0 * d1 / r
}

def integrate_r2(f: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    n = len(f)
    s = sum(f * r * r)
    s -= 0.5 * (f[0] * r[0] * r[0] + f[n - 1] * r[n - 1] * r[n - 1])
    return 4.0 * PI * h * s
}

def particle_number(rho: Arr, q, r: Arr, h) {
    return 4.0 * PI * h * sum(rho[q, :] * r * r)
}

def coulomb(rp: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    n = len(rp)
    out = zeros(n)
    #: charge inside r, over r
    inner = 0.0
    for i to n {
        inner += rp[i] * r[i] * r[i]
        out[i] = inner / r[i]
    }
    #: plus each outer shell's charge over its own radius
    outer = 0.0
    for k from 0 to n by 1 reversed {
        out[k] = E2 * 4.0 * PI * h * (out[k] + outer)
        outer += rp[k] * r[k]
    }
    return out
}

def proton_coulomb(rp: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    return coulomb(rp, r, h) - E2 * pow(3.0 / PI, 1.0 / 3.0) * pow(rp, 1.0 / 3.0)
}

def count_below(diag: Arr, off: Arr, x) {
    n = len(diag)
    cnt = 0
    #: Sturm count: the negative pivots in the factorization of T - x I
    p = diag[0] - x
    if p < 0.0 {
        cnt += 1
    }
    for i from 1 to n {
        if p == 0.0 {
            p = 1.0e-300
        }
        p = diag[i] - x - off[i - 1] * off[i - 1] / p
        if p < 0.0 {
            cnt += 1
        }
    }
    return cnt
}

def lowest_eigenvalue(diag: Arr, off: Arr, lo, hi) {
    a = lo
    b = hi
    while b - a > EIG_TOL {
        mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
        if count_below(diag, off, mid) > 0 {
            b = mid
        }
        else {
            a = mid
        }
    }
    return a
}

def inverse_iteration(diag: Arr, off: Arr, sigma, u: Arr) {
    n = len(diag)
    c = zeros(n)
    d = zeros(n)
    w = zeros(n)
    #: Thomas-algorithm solve, normalized along u
    for sweep to INV_SWEEPS {
        c[0] = off[0] / (diag[0] - sigma)
        d[0] = u[0] / (diag[0] - sigma)
        for i from 1 to n {
            m = diag[i] - sigma - off[i - 1] * c[i - 1]
            if i < n - 1 {
                c[i] = off[i] / m
            }
            d[i] = (u[i] - off[i - 1] * d[i - 1]) / m
        }
        w[n - 1] = d[n - 1]
        for k from 0 to n - 1 by 1 reversed {
            w[k] = d[k] - c[k] * w[k + 1]
        }
        nrm = sqrt(sum(w * w))
        if sum(w * u) < 0.0 {
            nrm = -nrm
        }
        u[:] = w / nrm
    }
    #: Rayleigh quotient
    lam = 0.0
    for i to n {
        lam += diag[i] * u[i] * u[i]
        if i < n - 1 {
            lam += 2.0 * off[i] * u[i] * u[i + 1]
        }
    }
    return lam
}

def skyrme_fields(f: SkyrmeForce, q, rho: Arr, tau: Arr, jso: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    step densities {
        rt = rho[NEUTRON, :] + rho[PROTON, :]
        tt = tau[NEUTRON, :] + tau[PROTON, :]
        jt = jso[NEUTRON, :] + jso[PROTON, :]
        rq = rho[q, :]
        sj = jt + jso[q, :]
        lap_t = lap_r(rt, r, h)
        drt = grad1(rt, h)
        lap_q = lap_r(rq, r, h)
        drq = grad1(rq, h)
        dsj = grad1(sj, h)
    }
    step effective_mass {
        B = HB + 0.125 * (f.t1 * (2.0 + f.x1) + f.t2 * (2.0 + f.x2)) * rt + 0.125 * (f.t2 * (1.0 + 2.0 * f.x2) - f.t1 * (1.0 + 2.0 * f.x1)) * rq
    }
    step central {
        ra = pow(rt, f.alpha)
        U = f.t0 * ((1.0 + f.x0 / 2.0) * rt - (f.x0 + 0.5) * rq)
        U += 0.25 * f.t1 * ((1.0 + f.x1 / 2.0) * (tt - 1.5 * lap_t) - (f.x1 + 0.5) * (tau[q, :] - 1.5 * lap_q))
        U += 0.25 * f.t2 * ((1.0 + f.x2 / 2.0) * (tt + 0.5 * lap_t) + (f.x2 + 0.5) * (tau[q, :] + 0.5 * lap_q))
        rsq = rho[NEUTRON, :] * rho[NEUTRON, :] + rho[PROTON, :] * rho[PROTON, :]
        U += f.t3 / 12.0 * ((1.0 + f.x3 / 2.0) * (2.0 + f.alpha) * ra * rt - (f.x3 + 0.5) * (2.0 * ra * rq + f.alpha * ra / rt * rsq))
        U -= f.w0 * (sj / r + 0.5 * dsj)
    }
    step spin_orbit {
        W = 0.5 * f.w0 * (drt + drq) + 0.125 * (f.t1 - f.t2) * jso[q, :] - 0.125 * (f.t1 * f.x1 + f.t2 * f.x2) * jt
    }
    return B, U, W
}

def skyrme_hamiltonian(B: Arr, dB: Arr, U: Arr, W: Arr, V: Arr, q, l, sdl, r: Arr, h) {
    nr = len(r)
    # B halfway between neighboring points; past the last point it meets HB
    bm = copy(B)
    bm[1:nr] = 0.5 * (B[0:nr - 1] + B[1:nr])
    bp = zeros(nr) + 0.5 * (B[nr - 1] + HB)
    bp[0:nr - 1] = 0.5 * (B[0:nr - 1] + B[1:nr])
    off = -bp[0:nr - 1] / (h * h)
    diag = (bm + bp) / (h * h) + B * l * (l + 1.0) / (r * r) + dB / r + U + sdl * W / r
    if q == PROTON {
        diag = diag + V
    }
    return diag, off
}

#| What skyrme_o16 finds: the energy per nucleon and the total energy
#| (MeV), the proton, neutron and charge radii (fm), the six orbital
#| energies (MeV: neutron 1s1/2, 1p3/2, 1p1/2, then the proton ones), the
#| number of passes and whether the energy settled in them, the mesh
#| points (fm), and the converged number, kinetic-energy and spin-orbit
#| densities, each `[2, nr]` (neutrons, then protons).
record SkyrmeO16 {
    e_per_a: Num
    energy: Num
    r_p: Num
    r_n: Num
    r_ch: Num
    levels: Arr
    iterations: Num
    converged: Bool
    r: Arr
    rho: Arr
    tau: Arr
    jso: Arr
}

def skyrme_o16(h, nr) -> SkyrmeO16 {
    return skyrme_hf(h, nr, SLY5, MIX, E_TOL, MAX_ITER)
}

def skyrme_hf(h, nr, force: SkyrmeForce, mix, e_tol, max_iter) -> SkyrmeO16 {
    nsh = len(SHELL_L)
    step mesh {
        r = zeros(nr)
        for i to nr {
            r[i] = (i + 1) * h
        }
    }
    step start {
        rho = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        tau = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        jso = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        prof = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp((r - WS_R0 * pow(A_NUC, 1.0 / 3.0)) / WS_DIFFUSE))
        pn = integrate_r2(prof, r, h)
        rho[NEUTRON, :] = prof * N_N / pn
        rho[PROTON, :] = prof * Z_P / pn
        # orbitals: warm-start vectors and last energies, block k = q * nsh + s
        uvec = zeros(NKIND * nsh, nr) + 1.0
        lam = zeros(NKIND * nsh)
        # the Coulomb field, which only protons feel
        V = zeros(nr)
        nrho = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        ntau = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        njso = zeros(NKIND, nr)
        e_old = 0.0
        E = 0.0
        it = 0
        done = 0
        # read by the debug lens only (skyrme_hf in skyrme.debug)
        de = 0.0
        n_neutrons = 0.0
        n_protons = 0.0
        split_n = 0.0
        split_p = 0.0
    }
    while done < 1 and it < max_iter {
        it += 1
        fill(nrho, 0.0)
        fill(ntau, 0.0)
        fill(njso, 0.0)
        for q to NKIND {
            step fields {
                B, U, W = skyrme_fields(force, q, rho, tau, jso, r, h)
                dB = grad1(B, h)
                if q == PROTON {
                    V = proton_coulomb(rho[PROTON, :], r, h)
                }
            }
            for s to nsh {
                step hamiltonian {
                    l = SHELL_L[s]
                    j = SHELL_J[s]
                    sdl = j * (j + 1.0) - l * (l + 1.0) - 0.75
                    diag, off = skyrme_hamiltonian(B, dB, U, W, V, q, l, sdl, r, h)
                }
                step diagonalize {
                    k = q * nsh + s
                    u = uvec[k, :]
                    sigma = lam[k] - NEAR
                    if it == 1 {
                        # Gershgorin: every eigenvalue lies within diag[i] +- (|off[i-1]| + |off[i]|)
                        big = max(abs(off))
                        sigma = lowest_eigenvalue(diag, off, min(diag) - 2.0 * big, max(diag) + 2.0 * big) - EIG_TOL
                    }
                    lam[k] = inverse_iteration(diag, off, sigma, u)
                }
                step occupy {
                    uvec[k, :] = u
                    R = u / (sqrt(h) * r)
                    dR = grad1(R, h)
                    wt = (2.0 * j + 1.0) / (4.0 * PI)
                    nrho[q, :] = nrho[q, :] + wt * R * R
                    ntau[q, :] = ntau[q, :] + wt * (dR * dR + l * (l + 1.0) / (r * r) * R * R)
                    njso[q, :] = njso[q, :] + wt * sdl / r * R * R
                }
            }
        }
        step mix {
            n_neutrons = particle_number(nrho, NEUTRON, r, h)
            n_protons = particle_number(nrho, PROTON, r, h)
            rho = (1.0 - mix) * rho + mix * nrho
            tau = (1.0 - mix) * tau + mix * ntau
            jso = (1.0 - mix) * jso + mix * njso
        }
        step energy {
            E = skyrme_energy(force, rho, tau, jso, r, h)
            de = E - e_old
            split_n = lam[NEUTRON * nsh + SHELL_P12] - lam[NEUTRON * nsh + SHELL_P32]
            split_p = lam[PROTON * nsh + SHELL_P12] - lam[PROTON * nsh + SHELL_P32]
        }
        step convergence {
            if abs(E - e_old) < e_tol and it > MIN_ITER {
                done = 1
            }
            e_old = E
        }
    }
    step observables {
        r2p = integrate_r2(rho[PROTON, :] * r * r, r, h) / Z_P
        r2n = integrate_r2(rho[NEUTRON, :] * r * r, r, h) / N_N
    }
    return SkyrmeO16 { e_per_a: E / A_NUC, energy: E, r_p: sqrt(r2p), r_n: sqrt(r2n), r_ch: sqrt(r2p + 1.5 * FOLD * FOLD), levels: lam, iterations: it, converged: done > 0, r: r, rho: rho, tau: tau, jso: jso }
}

def skyrme_energy(f: SkyrmeForce, rho: Arr, tau: Arr, jso: Arr, r: Arr, h) {
    rn = rho[NEUTRON, :]
    rp = rho[PROTON, :]
    rt = rn + rp
    drt = grad1(rt, h)
    drn = grad1(rn, h)
    drp = grad1(rp, h)
    tn = tau[NEUTRON, :]
    tp = tau[PROTON, :]
    tt = tn + tp
    jn = jso[NEUTRON, :]
    jp = jso[PROTON, :]
    jt = jn + jp
    rsq = rn * rn + rp * rp
    H = HB * tt + 0.5 * f.t0 * ((1.0 + f.x0 / 2.0) * rt * rt - (f.x0 + 0.5) * rsq)
    H += 0.25 * f.t1 * ((1.0 + f.x1 / 2.0) * (rt * tt + 0.75 * drt * drt) - (f.x1 + 0.5) * (rn * tn + 0.75 * drn * drn + rp * tp + 0.75 * drp * drp))
    H += 0.25 * f.t2 * ((1.0 + f.x2 / 2.0) * (rt * tt - 0.25 * drt * drt) + (f.x2 + 0.5) * (rn * tn - 0.25 * drn * drn + rp * tp - 0.25 * drp * drp))
    H += f.t3 / 12.0 * pow(rt, f.alpha) * ((1.0 + f.x3 / 2.0) * rt * rt - (f.x3 + 0.5) * rsq)
    H += (f.t1 - f.t2) / 16.0 * (jn * jn + jp * jp) - (f.t1 * f.x1 + f.t2 * f.x2) / 16.0 * jt * jt
    H += 0.5 * f.w0 * (jt * drt + jn * drn + jp * drp)
    #: Coulomb exchange in the Slater approximation
    ec = 0.5 * coulomb(rp, r, h) * rp - 0.75 * E2 * pow(3.0 / PI, 1.0 / 3.0) * pow(rp, 4.0 / 3.0)
    return integrate_r2(H, r, h) + integrate_r2(ec, r, h)
}

# ---- tests: the mesh tools on problems with known answers, and the whole
# solver against the post's numpy twin on its 0.1 fm mesh
SK_TEST_N = 40
SK_TEST_H = 0.1
SK_TWIN_H = 0.1
SK_TWIN_BOX = 15.0
# the numpy twin (posts/refs/skyrme-hartree-fock-of-oxygen-16.py) on the 0.1 fm
# mesh: E/A, the proton, neutron and charge radii, the neutron 1s1/2 1p3/2
# 1p1/2 energies and the proton ones
SK_TWIN = [-8.0465386180, 2.6809867361, 2.6558537301, 2.7966837288, -36.18659979, -20.63141616, -14.42364526, -32.38991872, -17.15296823, -11.07440402]

test "grad1 differentiates a quadratic exactly, at the two ends as well" {
    sk_x = zeros(SK_TEST_N)
    sk_f = zeros(SK_TEST_N)
    for i to SK_TEST_N {
        sk_x[i] = (i + 1) * SK_TEST_H
        sk_f[i] = 3.0 * sk_x[i] * sk_x[i] - sk_x[i]
    }
    assert_lt(max(abs(grad1(sk_f, SK_TEST_H) - (6.0 * sk_x - 1.0))), 1.0e-10)
}

test "bisection and inverse iteration find the lowest eigenvalue of the matrix with 2 on the diagonal and -1 beside it, 2 - 2 cos(pi / (n + 1))" {
    sk_diag = zeros(SK_TEST_N) + 2.0
    sk_off = zeros(SK_TEST_N - 1) - 1.0
    sk_exact = 2.0 - 2.0 * cos(PI / (SK_TEST_N + 1))
    sk_low = lowest_eigenvalue(sk_diag, sk_off, -1.0, 5.0)
    assert_near(sk_low, sk_exact, 1.0e-10)
    assert_near(count_below(sk_diag, sk_off, sk_exact + 1.0e-9), 1, 0.0)
    sk_u = zeros(SK_TEST_N) + 1.0
    assert_near(inverse_iteration(sk_diag, sk_off, sk_low - EIG_TOL, sk_u), sk_exact, 1.0e-12)
    assert_near(sum(sk_u * sk_u), 1.0, 1.0e-14)
}

test "on 150 points of 0.1 fm skyrme_o16 gives the post's numpy twin to 1e-7, in 38 iterations" {
    sk_res = skyrme_o16(SK_TWIN_H, round(SK_TWIN_BOX / SK_TWIN_H))
    sk_got = concat([sk_res.e_per_a, sk_res.r_p, sk_res.r_n, sk_res.r_ch], sk_res.levels)
    assert_lt(max(abs(sk_got - SK_TWIN)), 1.0e-7)
    assert_near(sk_res.iterations, 38, 0.0)
}
